messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected — elevated 5xx rate on /api/v1/generate and missing Datadog metric ingestion from eu-west-1 :rotating_light:
ops-bot: incident_id=INC-20260315-42, severity=sev2, paging on-call
Matt: seeing the same in the dashboard, but graphs are stuck loading — looks like some metrics aren't arriving :frowning:
Sasha: reported spikes from customer telemetry too. Are logs continuing to ingest?
Jin: I'm oncall. Checking log pipeline now.
Jin: logs are flowing to S3 and CloudWatch, but Datadog agent shows "ingest delay" and metric counts are flat since 1782001000
datadog-bot: Datadog status: "Partial service disruption in EU West region — metrics ingestion delayed" — https://status.datadoghq.com/incident/34567
Matt: ok, that's consistent. Primary problem: Datadog ingest delay causes blindspot for current incident. Need mitigation and alert hygiene.
Oliver: idea: switch critical alerting to CloudWatch aggregator and mute noisy Datadog alerts until we have metrics flowing. Also update status page.
Lia (Support): we already have two enterprise customers on tickets asking why alerts fired but the graphs are blank. I'll put a note in the ticket and escalate if needed.
Jin: plan: 1) suppress Datadog-generated anomalies to avoid pager storms 2) enable CloudWatch-based fallback alerts for key signals (5xx rate, request latency, queue depth) 3) enable more verbose local logging for affected services 4) handoff when rotation hits next oncall
Matt: I'll patch alert manager to route to cloudwatch-fallback receiver and add a silence for datadog-alerts for 30m.
Sasha: runbook snippet for CloudWatch fallback (copying to thread):
```
# enable cloudwatch fallback receiver
kubectl -n infra exec -it deploy/alertmanager -- alertmanagerctl silence add --matchers "alertname=High5xxRate" --timeout 30m
# update config to use cw-alerts for high-priority rules
kubectl -n infra apply -f /manifests/alerts/cw-fallback.yaml
```
Jin: I'll push the cw-fallback manifest and test with a synthetic 5xx spike (non-prod routing)
Matt: I'm adding a silence on the datadog alerting channel and reducing alert severity to warning for non-critical thresholds.
Oliver: support/status update draft: "We are currently experiencing delayed metric ingestion from Datadog in the EU-West region which may cause gaps in dashboards and delayed alerts. We are routing critical alarms to CloudWatch and are monitoring. Updates to follow." Want to post?
Lia (Support): post now and link to the incident thread + Datadog status. I'll monitor customer tickets.
Matt: posted to status.redwood.ai/incidents and #status-updates, added link to Datadog status page.
Jin: performed synthetic test — CloudWatch fallback alerted, receiver executed, confirmed routing to SRE oncall.
Sasha: any impact to Dedicated customers (reserved capacity)? Need to check if their monitoring is fully Datadog reliant.
Jin: quick check: Dedicated clusters in eu-west-1 have an extra exporter; I verified metrics there are available in CloudWatch. For hosted tenants relying solely on Datadog we'll have blindspots until Datadog resolves.
Lia (Support): escalated to customers on the two open tickets with the message and status link. They're asking for ETA; we don't have one yet.
Matt: mitigation checklist (added to incident notes): [x] silence noisy alerts in Datadog [x] enable CloudWatch fallbacks [x] increase local logging for critical services [x] post status update [ ] confirm end-to-end alerting for all customer classes [ ] restore Datadog silences and remove fallback once resolved
datadog-bot: update: "We have mitigations in place; ingestion rate improving but backfill in progress" — https://status.datadoghq.com/incident/34567/update-2
Sasha: seeing some metrics start to trickle in (latency graphs populating slowly). Backfill may show irregular data points for a bit.
Jin: re-run smoke queries and compare CloudWatch vs Datadog for discrepancy. attaching quick diff output:
```
# smoke query
SELECT avg(latency) FROM cw_metrics WHERE service='api' AND ts > now()-5m;
# datadog (slow)
SELECT avg(last) FROM dd_metrics WHERE metric='service.api.latency' AND ts > now()-20m;
```
Oliver: support asks if they should proactively call top customers. Lia — your call.
Lia (Support): I'm coordinating with account leads; will call three affected enterprise customers now.
Matt: once we see stable ingestion for 10m, we'll remove the Datadog silence and gradually shift back to primary alerting. Jin, please note when you hand off to next oncall.
Jin: noted. Handoff plan: I'll stay until 1782003600 then hand to @Oliver for monitoring. Leaving detailed runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/datadog-ingest-delay
Oliver: taking over at 1782003600. I'll watch alerts and customer comms. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Lia (Support): calling customers now, will update thread with any escalations.
Matt: incident summary draft for postmortem: root cause: third-party Datadog ingestion delay in eu-west-1 causing observability blindspots; mitigations: CloudWatch fallback, alert silencing and customer comms; action items: improve fallback automation, add synthetic checks for vendor ingestion, refine runbook handoffs.
datadog-bot: incident resolved: "Metrics ingestion restored and backfill complete" timestamp=1782004600 — https://status.datadoghq.com/incident/34567/resolved
Jin: confirmed backfill looks good. Restoring primary alerting and removing silences now.
Matt: removing cw-fallback manifests and Datadog silences cleared, monitoring for flurries.
Oliver: taking final watch and will close incident thread after 30m if stable.
Lia (Support): logged customer communication and closed one ticket; others pending confirmation.
ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-20260315-42 status=resolved, duration=~59m, severity=sev2
Oliver: thanks everyone. Postmortem next steps assigned in the doc.
